FIX THREE FOLLOW-UP REVIEW FINDINGS ON PR #798. Target branch codex/run-38011726130-1, expected head 7d12983; fail closed and write nothing if it moved. Only scripts/operator/actions/v3-derived-lifecycle-status.sh, tests/test_v3_derived_lifecycle_status.py and docs/operations/v3-finder-production-rollout-state.md may change.

F1 (P2, ~line 526): a missing v3_spatial.current_spatial_generation relation currently still satisfies current_pointers_recorded. On this production target the spatial pyramid is live and step 0 requires its pointer. FIX: current_pointers_recorded requires the canonical pointer row, the derived pointer row, AND that the spatial relation exists AND has a non-null current row. Missing relation or empty row -> failure code current_pointer_missing (status stopped). Update the existing spatial-absent test expectation accordingly (spatial absent is now a failure, not {'present': false} success) and keep reporting {'present': false} in the receipt for diagnosis.

F2 (P2, ~line 827): ready_for_governed_plan can be true even when a later query/df/mount step appended read_only_query_failed. FIX: compute migration_apply_preconditions as the LAST step before printing, with ready_for_governed_plan = all_named_workers_stopped and current_pointers_recorded and (failures is empty); also add 'inspection_complete': (failures is empty) to that section. Test: inject a failing footprint query (psql stub returns non-zero for the pg_database_size statement) and assert ready_for_governed_plan is false and status stopped.

F3 (P1, doc ~line 203): the disposable-sample section tells the operator to multiply only the body_mechanics/economy_opportunity TUPLE widths, omitting their primary-key indexes. Claude has now measured both relations the same way (replicated to ~200k rows with LIKE … INCLUDING ALL on PostgreSQL 18.4): body_mechanics 109 B/row table + 69 B/row index = 178 B/row total (199,800 sample rows); economy_opportunity 95 B/row table + 94 B/row index = 188 B/row total (199,908 sample rows); system_search in that re-run measured 273 B/row table + 164 B/row index = 438 B/row total (the earlier run gave 152 B/row index — GiST size varies a little between runs). FIX the doc: in the table add two rows for `body_mechanics` and `economy_opportunity` with those sample rows / table B/row / index B/row and 'n/a (scales with bodies / eligible body-economy pairs)' in the prod-rows and GB columns; change the system_search index B/row to 164 and total GB to 87 (273+164=437 B x 198.5M = 86.7 GB), the sum to about 1,174 GB; replace the sentence that quotes 104/89-byte tuples with: 'body_mechanics (178 B/row including its primary key) and economy_opportunity (188 B/row including its primary key) scale with bodies and eligible body/economy pairs, not systems; multiply those totals by the production row counts the step 0 receipt reports (`footprint.relations`, `n_live_tup`) for the published generation and add the result to the sum above.' Keep everything else in that section.

VALIDATION: 1. bash -n the script  2. python -m pytest tests/test_v3_derived_lifecycle_status.py -q -p no:cacheprovider  3. ruff on the extracted heredoc body  4. git diff --name-only 7d12983 lists only the three allowed files. Commit message: 'ops: step 0 readiness requires the spatial pointer and a clean inspection; body-table index bytes in the footprint note'.
